ai_show_review.summary: Acoustic jam on Mountains of the Moon, fiery Lovelight
ai_show_review.blurb: The set is a compact festival‑style burst featuring Pigpen’s powerhouse Turn On Your Lovelight and an unexpected acoustic jam on Mountains Of The Moon. Jerry’s SG work shines while Phil anchors the groove. A tight three‑song outing that captures the free‑wheeling spirit of late ’68.
ai_show_review.review:
On December 20, 1968 at the Shrine Exposition Hall, the Dead delivered a brief but potent set that still feels fresh for listeners today. Kicking off with The Eleven, they moved straight into an acoustic exploration of Mountains Of The Moon – Jerry Garcia’s fluid SG solo weaving through the melody while Phil Lesh provides a solid bass foundation. Pigpen then takes center stage for a raucous Turn On Your Lovelight, his gritty vocals and harmonica cutting through the mix and driving the crowd wild. The soundboard capture from Miller preserves the energy of the performance; despite a faint tape hiss it offers clear instrument separation that lets the nuances of the acoustic jam and Pigpen’s vocal fireworks shine.

Both available recordings highlight the same musical peaks, but the Miller SBD version stands out for its fidelity and completeness, making it the go‑to source for anyone wanting to hear this late‑’68 snapshot. Whether you’re a completist or just hunting great early Dead moments, this show’s combination of folk‑rock tightness, improvisational bravery, and Pigpen’s charismatic command makes it well worth a listen.

best_recording.reason: Good‑quality soundboard capture with clear instrument separation; preserves the acoustic jam and Lovelight energy despite minor tape hiss.
